data.one_liner: A CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) library providing an IPv4/v6 client in Dart.
data.what_it_does: It implements the Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) for resource-constrained networks and nodes. It provides a CoAP client supporting UDP, observe resources, block-wise transfers, and custom methods like FETCH and PATCH.
use_when: You need to communicate with IoT devices using the CoAP protocol.
You need support for CoAP over UDP, block-wise transfers, or observing resources.
avoid_when: You are communicating with standard REST APIs over HTTP or HTTPS.
You require robust background connectivity without manually managing app lifecycle states.
strengths: Full implementation of an IPv4/6 CoAP client with RFC compliance.
Supports advanced features like block-wise transfers, observe resources, and multicast over UDP.
weaknesses: Futures may not survive when the app runs in the background or screen is off without manual lifecycle handling.
DTLS support is experimental and requires shipping OpenSSL binaries for platforms like iOS and Windows.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding dependencies and running build_runner to generate the configuration class from a YAML file. DTLS usage requires native OpenSSL binaries on certain platforms.
